trust_decision.summary: Text taken from the recipe input (Series chart columns) is untrusted and may not name a prototype slot when the chart's series map is built, and objects handed to the shared protocol table renderer must contribute only their own keys, HTML-escaped. Both halves are decided in libraries: getSeriesValues in src/core/lib/Charts.mjs builds the nested map, and objToTable in src/core/lib/Protocol.mjs renders any parsed-packet object to HTML.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the Series chart operation, so an engineer greps SeriesChart and lands on `series[serie][xVal] = val`: the classic unbounded-key write where a first column of `__proto__` writes the second column straight onto Object.prototype.

fix_sites.entry_point: Parse UDP present (src/core/operations/ParseUDP.mjs:83), Parse TCP present (src/core/operations/ParseTCP.mjs:149), Parse TLS record present (src/core/operations/ParseTLSRecord.mjs:104)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/core/lib/Protocol.mjs:18-41 (objToTable), consumed by ParseUDP.mjs:83, ParseTCP.mjs:149 and ParseTLSRecord.mjs:104

O3_reason_to_dismiss: objToTable is generic packet-table formatting for UDP/TCP/TLS present() views; it never sees chart code or chart arguments, so an engineer anchoring on 'prototype pollution in Series Chart' reads the request to change it as an unrelated renderer concern, especially once the pollution source in Charts.mjs is fixed.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A series or x-axis label literally named `__proto__` (or `constructor`) is legal chart data and must keep showing as an own series/x value, so a fix that deletes or skips those names silently drops real data; likewise objToTable must keep recursing into nested objects, because Parse TCP's Options and each option's Value render as sub-tables.

O6_input_shapes: series name (column 1) equal to `__proto__` - reaches the outer map write at Charts.mjs:166, where a plain `{}` already returns Object.prototype instead of undefined
x value (column 2) equal to `__proto__` - reaches the inner map write at Charts.mjs:167
x value containing inline HTML (``) - renders as a raw key in objToTable
a key inherited from a polluted Object.prototype with no matching own property - skipped by Object.keys at Protocol.mjs:28 and Charts.mjs:173
null values - previously marched into the object branch, now treated as a scalar and stringified
non-string scalar values (numbers, booleans, undefined) - coerced with String() before escaping (src/core/lib/Protocol.mjs:36, fix.diff:66)
nested objects - still recursed as sub-tables rather than flattened

O7_producer.where: src/core/lib/Charts.mjs:147-179 (getSeriesValues maps CSV rows into {seriesName: {xValue: number}}) - the renderer's own-key filter at src/core/lib/Protocol.mjs:28 never calls it and shares no state with it; the only link between producer and sink is global Object.prototype

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second options map whose keys are wire-supplied names (unknown TCP option kind echoed as the key) instead of the fixed lookup name
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Parse TCP already builds `options[opt.name] = option` from a kind lookup at 100-123 and hands the object to objToTable at 149, so widening the lookup fallback to echo the observed Kind is a small, natural change that recreates the user-keyed object.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third chart builder that groups scatter points by a user-supplied colour/label column the way getSeriesValues groups by column 1
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already holds three builders that differ only in how many columns they read (getValues, getScatterValues, getScatterValuesWithColour), so a maintainer adding a grouped scatter or heatmap label would key objects by input text in the same shape.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A sibling renderer (e.g. objToDefinitionList or a YAML/table variant) copied from objToTable for a new protocol parser
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: objToTable is the house style for every packet parser's present(); a new protocol operation copying this 20-line function would repeat the for...in loop and the unescaped template literals unless the pattern is fixed in the shared helper.

O9_family: prototype pollution (CWE-1321) chained into HTML injection / XSS (CWE-79) through an unescaped object-to-table renderer

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=24 <25 (package.json:213-215); npm + grunt + webpack; `npx grunt configTests` then `node tests/node/index.mjs` and `node tests/operations/index.mjs` (package.json:200); node_modules is not present in the tree, so npm install is needed once before the build
O10_build.project_tests: tests/operations/tests/Charts.mjs:34-43 (Series chart smoke test) and tests/operations/tests/Charts.mjs:45-54 (Series chart escapes x-axis values in serialized SVG, pre-existing); tests/operations/tests/ParseUDP.mjs, ParseTCP.mjs and ParseTLSRecord.mjs cover run() output only; there is no test for src/core/lib/Protocol.mjs at the pinned commit (no tests/**/*Protocol*) and the fix's tests/node/tests/lib/ChartsProtocolPrototypePollution.mjs does not exist in the pinned tree

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Stop the __proto__ series name at the landing point - skip or rename rows whose series/x value is __proto__, or swap the plain map for a Map/filtered object in getSeriesValues - and never touch objToTable's for...in loop or its unescaped template literals.

out_of_scope_notes: src/core/operations/ToTable.mjs:180-187 writes CSV cells into HTML without escaping; a reflected XSS with no relation to prototype pollution, outside this advisory.

src/core/operations/ExtractID3.mjs:153-156 and src/core/operations/TextEncodingBruteForce.mjs:81-83 are different object-to-HTML renderers that also loop with for...in and emit the key unescaped, so a polluted Object.prototype would surface there too; they are not the Protocol.mjs sink and the published fix did not touch them.

src/core/operations/ParseTLSRecord.mjs:34-36 iterates ContentType with for...in inside the constructor, so a polluted prototype also writes into this._contentTypes; noticed while tracing objToTable's callers, not pursued.
